# Bash Guidelines
https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html

## Purpose
Rules for writing and reviewing Bash scripts. Target: **Bash 5.3** (current GNU release). Many systems still ship older versions (Bash 5.2 on most Linux distributions, Bash 3.2 as `/bin/bash` on macOS), so:
- Write for **Bash 5.x** by default.
- Use Bash 5.3-only features (`${ cmd; }`, `${| cmd; }`, `GLOBSORT`) only when the script checks the version (`(( BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 5 || (BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 5 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 3) ))`) or the runtime is known to have 5.3.
- Write POSIX `sh` only when the file uses `#!/bin/sh`; then no Bash features at all.

## Script header
- Start every script with:
  ```bash
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -Eeuo pipefail
  shopt -s inherit_errexit nullglob
  IFS=$'\n\t'
  ```
- Follow with a short comment block: purpose, usage, required environment variables, exit codes.
- Resolve the script directory with `script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"`; never rely on the caller's working directory.
- Add `trap cleanup EXIT` for temporary files and `trap 'on_error $LINENO' ERR` for useful error messages.

## Structure
- Put all logic in functions and end the script with `main "$@"`.
- Declare function variables with `local`; declare constants with `readonly` in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
- Names: `snake_case` for functions and local variables, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for exported environment variables and constants.
- Parse options with `getopts` (short options) or a `while (( $# )); case "$1" in` loop (long options); always provide `-h`/`--help` with a `usage()` function.
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` general error, `2` usage error; document others.

## Quoting and variables
- Always double-quote expansions: `"$var"`, `"${array[@]}"`, `"$(command)"`. The only exceptions are inside `[[ ]]` and `(( ))` where word splitting doesn't apply.
- Use `${var}` braces when concatenating; `${var:-default}` for defaults; `${var:?message}` for required variables.
- Use arrays for lists and command arguments (`args=(--flag "$value"); cmd "${args[@]}"`), never space-separated strings.
- Use `$(...)` for command substitution, never backticks.
- Use `declare -A` for associative arrays and `mapfile -t` / `readarray -t` to read lines into arrays.

## Conditionals and arithmetic
- Use `[[ ... ]]` for tests, never `[ ... ]` or `test` in Bash scripts. Use `==` and `=~` inside `[[ ]]`; keep regexes in a variable.
- Use `(( ... ))` for arithmetic and numeric comparisons, never `expr` or `let`.
- Check commands directly (`if grep -q pattern file; then`), not via `$?`.
- Use `command -v tool >/dev/null` to check dependencies at the start of the script, and fail with a clear message.

## Loops and files
- Iterate over files with globs (`for f in "$dir"/*.log`), never by parsing `ls` output.
- Read files line by line with `while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < "$file"`.
- Handle file names with spaces and newlines: use `find ... -print0 | xargs -0` or `find ... -exec ... {} +`, and `read -d ''` for NUL-separated input.
- Create temporary files and directories with `mktemp` / `mktemp -d` and remove them in the `EXIT` trap.
- Use `printf '%s\n'` instead of `echo` for data or anything with variables; `echo` only for fixed messages.
- Send errors and diagnostics to stderr: `printf 'Error: %s\n' "$msg" >&2`.

## Bash 5.3 features (only with a version check or known runtime)
- `${ cmd; }` runs a command substitution in the current shell (no subshell, variables persist) — use it for performance-critical loops instead of `$(...)`.
- `${| cmd; }` captures the value of `REPLY` set by `cmd`, for functions that return values without printing.
- `GLOBSORT` controls sort order of glob results (e.g. `GLOBSORT=-mtime` for newest first) instead of `ls -t` parsing.

## Security
- Never use `eval` or build commands from strings; never pass unvalidated input to `sh -c` or `bash -c`.
- Never hardcode secrets; read them from environment variables or a secret store, and never print them (`set +x` around sensitive sections).
- Use `--` to end options before user-supplied arguments (`rm -- "$file"`).
- Guard destructive commands: `rm -rf -- "${dir:?}"/*` so an empty variable can't expand to `/`.
- Download with `curl --fail --silent --show-error --location` and verify checksums; never pipe remote scripts straight into `bash`.
- Set `umask 077` when creating files with sensitive content.

## Portability
- Use `/usr/bin/env bash` in the shebang so a newer Bash on `PATH` is used (important on macOS).
- Prefer POSIX options of external tools; note GNU-only options (`sed -i`, `date -d`, `readlink -f`) and provide a macOS/BSD alternative where the script must run there.
- Avoid Bash features newer than the documented minimum version of the script.

## Testing and quality
- Lint every script with ShellCheck (`shellcheck -x`) with zero warnings; add `# shellcheck disable=SCxxxx` only with a comment explaining why.
- Format with `shfmt -i 2 -ci -bn` (or the project's `.editorconfig`).
- Test with Bats (`bats-core`) for scripts with logic beyond a few commands.
- Make scripts idempotent where possible (safe to run twice), and support a `--dry-run` option for destructive operations.

## Code review focus
Flag in this order: unquoted expansions, `eval` or string-built commands, missing `set -Eeuo pipefail`, unguarded `rm -rf`, parsing `ls` output, secrets in scripts or logs, missing dependency checks, Bash 5.3 features without a version check, ShellCheck warnings.
